entry.title: Jeep Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept Truck
entry.summary: The Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept reimagines the CJ-8 pickup as a high-speed desert truck, and it is the first desert-performance Jeep concept with SRT badging. Built on a Wrangler chassis, the body is reshaped from the windshield back: longer doors, an open pickup bed, a new ta
entry.content:
The Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept reimagines the CJ-8 pickup as a high-speed desert truck, and it is the first desert-performance Jeep concept with SRT badging. Built on a Wrangler chassis, the body is reshaped from the windshield back: longer doors, an open pickup bed, a new tailgate and a roll cage. Details include bronze beadlock wheels, oversized tires and Punk'n orange paint, along with a fresh take on the Sharknose front end. Its independent front suspension, a first for the Wrangler, was developed with off-road racer Casey Currie and borrows from the Striker concept's setup, while the rear axle takes cues from trophy trucks. The back seats hook into the floor. They can rotate to face backward or come out and leave the whole bed free for hauling.

The Pro's Closet makes buying and selling pre-owned bikes easier, bringing a more trustworthy, hassle-free experience to the secondhand market. With more than 80,000 bikes bought and sold, the platform puts every ride through its Certified Pre-Owned tuning process before it ships, helping riders find quality road, mountain, and gravel bikes without paying full retail. Selling is just as straightforward, while a 30-day return policy and dedicated Ride Guide team add peace of mind. Each bike arrives in a purpose-built Ride Fast Shipping box designed to simplify assembly, making it easier to get back on the road or trail. For riders looking to upgrade, cash out, or find their next great ride, The Pro's Closet makes the used-bike market feel like new.

Stefan Amato, founder of the adventure cycling hub Pannier.cc, has curated tours for over a decade. In Grand Bikepacking Journeys, he takes on iconic routes like Nepal's Annapurna Circuit, Vietnam's Ha Giang Loop, South Africa's Cross Cape, the Trans-Pyrenees between France and Spain and the Iditarod across Alaska. Each route gets its history and geography, along with practical advice on planning, gear and handling the challenges of the ride. The 272-page hardcover is aimed at riders of every level.

entry.content:

A distinctive collectible that brings together two American cultural traditions.

entry.content:
Bravo Sierra spent two years developing its first eau de parfum, Vanilla Hide. While the name suggests vanilla, the formulation doesn't actually contain it. Instead, tea and spice achieve this unique fragrance. Top notes of mandarin zest, coriander seed, and pink pepper add sharpness over a dry heart of black tea, violet leaf, and sueded rose. A base of amber, vetiver, and patchouli develops an underlying warm structure. Due to the eau de parfum's higher concentration of fragrance oil, it lasts longer on skin than the lower oil ratios in traditional cologne. The fragrance is made in New York, and part of every sale supports veterans and their families through Semper Fi & America's Fund.

entry.content:

Each is set up for a different winter job. The Tundra is the mobile basecamp, and its top rack drops down so gear is easier to load. The Tacoma carries an awning and recovery gear for tight trails, the Land Cruiser a ski rack, and the 4Runner and Sequoia Thule cargo boxes. They are prototypes that Toyota says may not be allowed on public roads, perhaps an acceptable limitation for vehicles built to cross deep snow.

entry.content:
In addition to being emissions-free, electric powertrains allow for exploration of the outdoors without the noise created by ICE-powered transports. For snowy locales, Moonbikes provides a solid option with their electric snowmobile. It has an innovative propulsion system that is both highly efficient and totally silent, with a top speed of 26 mph and the ability to handle powder up to 12 inches deep. The low center gravity and modest weight — under 200 lbs with a single battery — make it extremely easy to ride, while the 28-inch width makes it easy to transport. It can run up to 1.5 hours with a single battery in temperatures as low as -13°F and is assembled in France by Bosch. Ready for adventure wherever you can find snow, it ships in 1-2 weeks with a single battery and standard charger.
